That is to say, clearing the bacterium with antimicrobial therapy produced lasting remission of peptic ulcers. This pattern of cure, reproduced across trial populations, converted a contested hypothesis into standard gastroenterological practice, and institutional recognition followed only after that therapeutic result was firmly on record.
